title: Making AI-Enhanced Videos: Analyzing Generative AI Use Cases in YouTube Content Creation
venue: Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI EA '25)
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how generative AI tools are being used in YouTube video creation. The authors note that tools such as ChatGPT, MidJourney, Leonardo.AI, and ElevenLabs are increasingly adopted by content creators, but specific use cases across the full video-production workflow are not yet well documented. The study therefore asks how creators use generative AI during planning, production, editing, and uploading of videos.

To answer this question, the authors collected YouTube how-to videos using the YouTube Data API and analyzed a final dataset of 274 English-language videos posted between September 2023 and February 2024. They used transcript segmentation and thematic analysis to identify recurring use cases of generative AI. The resulting framework maps uses across four phases: planning (e.g., identifying topics, scripting), production (e.g., prompt refinement, generating images, avatars, voiceovers, music), editing (e.g., lip-syncing, restyling, upscaling, clipping, translation), and uploading (e.g., subtitles, title generation).

The population studied is not students or teachers in formal education settings, but YouTube creators and the broader online creator community as represented through publicly available how-to videos. The context is online content creation rather than schooling or classroom learning. The empirical material consists of videos and their transcripts, not direct educational participants or intervention recipients.

The main conclusion is that generative AI is already embedded across many stages of creator workflows and is used not only for content generation but also for editing and publishing support. The authors propose a conceptual framework of these use cases and discuss implications for future HCI research, including creativity, prompting skill, authenticity of AI-generated content, accessibility, and transparency around AI-assisted media. This is not a randomized educational trial, does not involve high-school writing instruction, and provides no motivation or writing outcome statistics relevant to ChatGPT-based school interventions.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/descriptive content-analysis study with a clear method, sampling procedure, and inter-rater reliability, but it is not an educational experiment and provides no causal evidence on student outcomes. It meets only limited credibility criteria for the K-12 intervention framework.
impact_tier_rationale: The study suggests potentially beneficial workflow/productivity uses of GenAI for creators, but impact is descriptive and unclear, with no effect sizes or educational outcome gains. Therefore impact cannot be judged as demonstrated positive impact in the synthesis framework.

interventions.use_case: Qualitative analysis of how YouTube creators use generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, MidJourney, Gemini, ElevenLabs, and video-generation/editing tools across planning, production, editing, and uploading phases of social media video creation.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports descriptive qualitative evidence that YouTube creators use generative AI to streamline video-production workflow tasks such as scriptwriting, prompt refinement, image/video generation, voiceover creation, editing, subtitling, and title generation. No experimental comparison, learner outcomes, or causal effect sizes are reported; the evidence consists of frequencies of use cases across 274 analyzed how-to videos rather than impact estimates.
finding.measure: Frequency and thematic prevalence of GenAI use cases in YouTube how-to videos across planning, production, editing, and uploading stages

finding.finding_summary: This paper does not study educational achievement, writing performance, motivation, or any K-12 learning outcome. It is focused on creator practices in social media video production, so there are no original statistics relevant to student writing or school-based ChatGPT interventions.
